Subject: Follow-up from today — TTFT & streaming requirements

Hi team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful discussion. Quick recap of our perf/streaming needs and where we are looking for alignment: 

- Primary goal: conversational search widgets across our product with interactive streaming replies.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 120 ms for single-turn prompts (50-200 token responses).
- Streaming: SSE or WebSocket preferred; chunk cadence ideally 50-100 ms (small chunks for perceived responsiveness).
- Concurrency & throughput: baseline 200 concurrent users, peak 600 concurrent, average QPS ~180; expect variance by region.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile of TTFT <= 150 ms; tail behavior is important for user experience.
- Data/PKG: we can provide representative prompt mixes and sample payloads.

Open questions we discussed that would help us qualify:
1) Do you recommend Hosted vs Dedicated for these TTFT targets at our scale?
2) What streaming cadence can Redwood guarantee for SSE/WebSocket out of the box?
3) Any special model/quantization recommendations to hit TTFT without sacrificing quality?

Next steps from our side: we will share a sample prompt set and traffic shape by EOD tomorrow. From Redwood, would appreciate a short mutual action plan and a proposed POC scope.

Thanks,
Sam Rivera
Staff Product Manager — Search & Recommendations
Acme Retail

Hi Sam — great to talk earlier. Quick recap from our side + proposed next steps.

Recap (agreeing with your bullets):
- Target TTFT <= 120 ms; SLO target p95 <= 150 ms.
- Streaming via SSE/WebSocket acceptable; target cadence 50-100 ms per chunk.
- Concurrency baseline 200 / peak 600.

What Redwood recommends (high level):
- For aggressive TTFT (<=120 ms) at your concurrency, Dedicated capacity is the safest path — predictable GPUs, reserved batches, and low-noise neighbors. Hosted can work for smaller pilots but may require tuning and fallbacks.
- Streaming cadence: we support both SSE and WebSockets. We can configure chunk flush intervals at ~50-100 ms depending on batching and model behavior. We'll propose a recommended chunk size/cadence during the POC.
- Model selection: open-weights LLMs with optimized kernels + 8-bit quantization are usually the best tradeoff. We'll run a short benchmark (sample payloads) to recommend a specific model/quant profile.

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan (short MVP scope):
1) You share sample prompts, average/peak QPS shape, and a few representative long/short responses (EOD tomorrow).
2) Redwood runs a 72-hour benchmark: TTFT & streaming cadence tests across Hosted + Dedicated (if you want dedicated numbers we can include a rough cost estimate).
3) We deliver a results document with recommended model + quantization profile, expected TTFT/throughput curves, and an SLO proposal.
4) POC kickoff (remote) to validate in your env OR our dedicated cluster.

I attached a short TTFT checklist and our SLO template to make it easy for your infra team to share the traffic shape.

Would Wednesday 07/22 at 10am PT work for a 30-min POC kickoff to review the benchmark plan?

Thanks — will coordinate with Dev & Marcus on the technical plan.

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — TTFT & streaming requirements (technical notes)

Hi Sam / Marissa —

A few technical notes to set expectations before the benchmark:

- Achieving TTFT <= 120 ms depends on three levers: model latency (kernels/sequence length), serving stack (dedicated GPUs, pre-warmed KV cache), and networking (idle connection warm-up for WebSocket/SSE).

- At your concurrency (~200-600), Dedicated + reserved worker pool with persistent processes will reduce cold-starts and provide the most consistent tail latency.

- Streaming chunk cadence: we control flush frequency at the runtime layer. When using autoregressive decoding, small token flushes every 50-100 ms are achievable if the model generates tokens quickly; for some models token generation time > 40ms/token which limits cadence. We'll measure tokens/sec on your sample prompts.

- Quantization: 8-bit (GPTQ / AWQ-style) typically gives substantial latency improvements with near-identical output for many workloads. We'll include both FP16 & 8-bit runs in the benchmark.

- Concurrency math (quick back-of-envelope): if median token gen time is 30 ms/token and average response is 60 tokens, median generation time ~1.8s — however TTFT primarily measures generation of the first token; with caching and pre-tokenization we can target first-token time << total generation. We'll instrument to isolate TTFT (network + model first-token).

Actionables from Redwood engineering:
- Please upload sample prompt set and traffic shapes to the Drive link Marissa shared.
- We'll provision a small dedicated cluster and run: p95 TTFT, p99 TTFT, streaming chunk cadence distribution, and throughput vs concurrency curves for FP16 and 8-bit.
- Expect initial benchmark results within 72 hrs of receiving samples.

Happy to jump on the kickoff Wed 07/22 10am PT to walk through the benchmark plan and scope.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Software Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
